questions.q: Which scan accurately checks for missing patches on a host?
questions.explain: An authenticated scan uses credentials to read the actual system state. An unauthenticated scan only sees the network surface.

questions.q: Which tool answers the question 'does the detected IP address belong to an authorized asset?'
questions.explain: IPAM manages the address inventory and assignments. CSPM covers cloud configuration, not IP addressing. Concept from objective 4.3 (beyond textbooks).

questions.q: Which elements should be factored into vulnerability prioritization? (Select all that apply)
questions.explain: Prioritization combines technical severity, exposure, and criticality. Alphabetical order has no bearing on risk.

questions.q: An EOL product can no longer be patched. What action is expected?
options: Document the exception with a compensating control and owner approval
Wait for the next annual scan
questions.explain: Risk acceptance is an explicit, compensated, and reviewed decision. A false positive is a detection error, not a choice.

questions.q: Match each phase to its characteristic action.

pairs.right: Authenticated scan, IPAM, CSPM, code review
Severity assessment and pentest report review

questions.explain: Each phase has a distinct deliverable: discovery, ranking, remediation, and proof of closure.

options: Publishing the exploit immediately after discovery
Reporting through a dedicated channel and allowing a remediation window before publication
Selling the flaw to the highest bidder without notifying the vendor
questions.explain: Responsible disclosure structures reporting, protects the researcher, and gives time to patch before any publication. Concept from objective 4.3 (beyond textbooks).
